name: Chipply
description: Online team stores for the decorated-apparel trade: custom jerseys, spiritwear, and fan gear. It grew out of a family sporting-goods store that has been around since 1881. Chipply takes a percentage of sales. They are adding a fuller "run the dealership" product.

mentions.evidence: Company-stated, Practical Founders, September 2026. About $10M revenue this year. Processing around $250M of merchandise. About 1,500 active dealers. About 50 employees. Growing about 35%. Started in 2015, selling since 2018. Growth equity from Growth Street Partners. The founders kept control.
mentions.indieAngle: Take a cut of the order in a trade a generic shop cannot handle.

whyItPrints: A team order is sizes, decorations, and a dealer in the middle. A generic shop template does not do that. When a parent orders, the dealer and Chipply both get paid on the unit.
whyThisMatters:
Chipply is the online store for a dealer who decorates team apparel: jerseys, spiritwear, fan gear. It grew out of a family sporting-goods store that opened in 1881. Chipply takes a percentage of the sale, so it gets paid when the dealer gets paid. They are adding a fuller product for running the dealership.

About ten million in revenue this year, on about two hundred and fifty million of merchandise going through. About fifteen hundred dealers. About fifty people. Growing about thirty-five percent. Selling since 2018. They took growth equity and kept control. September 2026. Self-reported.

You pay as a cut of the order, because a generic shop cannot handle the sizes and the decoration.

The percentage of sales is the pricing model, so a bigger dealer order is a bigger Chipply bill. Two hundred and fifty million is merchandise going through, not Chipply revenue. The ten million is the revenue line. Growth Street Partners is the equity partner, and the founders say they kept control. The family store dates to 1881. Selling started in 2018.
